## Introduction

First, I started this assignment by recreating the code in Chapter 2 of Text Mining with R. I had to download numerous libraries and text packages to get the code working properly. It was very useful to recreate the code and helped with my understanding.

For the extension of the assignment, I plan to select articles from various news outlet to understand their sentiment towards the midterms elections. I plan to create a visual showing which news outlets had neutral, negative, and positive sentiment towards the election.

To gather the data, I plan to use Claude Code to scrap the articles from the web. As well, recommend a non-bias lexicon. Choosing the wrong lexicon could create bias in my results, i.e. positive sentiment could be mistaken for neutral.

## Approach

I will first start the assignment by recreating Chapter 2 of Text Mining with R. This will allow me to better understand the basics of sentiment analysis before taking on an advanced example.

After, I will prompt Claude to gather news articles about the recent midterm elections, and extract the text to be used in R. I want about 15 different news outlets, some that are local to Albany, Poughkeepsie, NYC and national news outlets. I want the news outlets to span the entire political spectrum.

For this project, I will also need a non-bias lexcon which I will research using Claude, and I will focus heavily on reviewing this document.

Last, I will conduct the sentiment analysis and create a few visualizations. I expect some challenges web scrapping the articles due to CSS formatting.

## Reproducing

```{r Reproducing Chapter 2}
library(janeaustenr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidytext)

tidy_books <- austen_books() %>%
  group_by(book) %>%
  mutate(
    linenumber = row_number(),
    chapter = cumsum(str_detect(text, 
                                regex("^chapter [\\divxlc]", 
                                      ignore_case = TRUE)))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, text)

nrc_joy <- get_sentiments("nrc") %>% 
  filter(sentiment == "joy")

tidy_books %>%
  filter(book == "Emma") %>%
  inner_join(nrc_joy) %>%
  count(word, sort = TRUE)
```
